title: Sore lips from high notes; other players' lip trouble
summary: He explains how hard high-note work injured Pinkett, Cad and others, and trombonist Clement's good lip.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: I think Pickett had the same trouble. Pickett had the same trouble too. That's right. Yeah.

Well, Pinkett too had the same trouble over there. That's how Pinkett had quit the job. And the Pinkett quit. After Pinkett quit, Cad went back there and Cad got the same trouble. Now Alvin told me that's when Alvin no one wake over there. Man do you know. Now Thomas. Of course this time, Thomas had to go down this time blow it up on Thomas. Thomas did have that you let blow down on him one time. Uh huh. You hitin' them high notes like that. You can't be hitin' them high notes like that. Yeah. It's gonna spoil your left hand. Playing on, you know, on the system. I've seen him play all night and then go on the parade all day.

That's right. That's right. He got a good lip I guess. He got a good lip with it. Clemmon plays that horn. No impression. No impression. No impression.
